source.title: Kronecker Factorization Improves Efficiency and Interpretability of Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Vadim Kurochkin; Yaroslav Aksenov; Daniil Laptev; Daniil Gavrilov; Nikita Balagansky

record.tranche_reason: The study refines how polysemanticity should be interpreted: one SAE pre-latent has different semantic patterns at different activation magnitudes, while its composed post-latents are more specific. This bears on V7's activation-range qualification, though it does not study the original vision-neuron examples.
record.gate_note: The study analyzes sparse-autoencoder latents, not MLP neuron response counts. Its reconstruction, interpretability-score, absorption, and correlation results do not directly measure the versions' stated neuron polysemanticity. The included row records the explicit activation-range analysis relevant to V7; the paper does not compare explanation-scoring methods.
record.test_reason: The study builds a new sparse autoencoder (KronSAE) and reports its reconstruction, compute, absorption and interpretability performance. SAEs are motivated by polysemantic, superposed model features, so the study relies on the finding as background, but it never measures polysemanticity of the language model's own neurons. The one polysemanticity observation is about the SAE's own pre-latents. The authors attribute it to the SAE's reduced encoder capacity, an artifact of their design. That is a different kind of system from the network neurons the versions name.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that KronSAE matches TopK SAE on the EV–FLOPs frontier, reduces absorption and yields more specific, interpretable post-latents. Pre-latents can be polysemous, which they expect from reduced encoder capacity. They hypothesize some semantics are encoded in activation magnitude, checked only qualitatively on activation examples; they note dataset or interpretation artifacts cannot be ruled out.
record.recipe_differences: This is a factorized sparse-autoencoder study with qualitative latent interpretation and activation-range analysis, not a reproduction of the original neuron-visualization or neuron-response method.
record.method_sensitivity: The semantic interpretation of the example pre-latent differs across activation-magnitude ranges.

fits_no_version.finding: A KronSAE base pre-latent (Gemma-2-2B layer 12, base 3, head 23) carries three distinct semantics: comparison, spiritual and geographical. These appear to separate by activation magnitude. Its AND-compositions with extension pre-latents give more specific post-latents with scores up to 0.93. The authors attribute the polysemanticity to reduced encoder capacity in the factorized SAE.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Capacity-reduced SAE encoder latents become polysemantic, with distinct semantics partly separable by activation magnitude; composing them via AND yields more specific features.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The relevant activation-range result is a qualitative example rather than a prevalence estimate; the paper notes that interpretation or dataset artifacts cannot be ruled out without further validation. The study concerns SAE latents, not individual transformer neurons.
record.rows_left_out: Reconstruction-fidelity, FLOP, absorption, correlation, and aggregate interpretability results in Sections 4–6 and the appendices were left out because they do not directly measure the claim versions' neuron polysemanticity or activation-range classification dependence.

untested.parts: Image-classifier neurons responding to unrelated visual inputs; no vision models studied.
Share of polysemantic MLP neurons in transformer LMs and layer differences; SAEs are trained on residual streams and model neurons are not analyzed.
Superposition as the cause of neuron polysemanticity; not tested (the toy model only checks correlation-structure recovery by SAEs).
Polysemanticity arising without capacity pressure; not tested.
Dependence of neuron polysemanticity share on activation function, architecture or regularization; only SAE architectures are varied, not the model's.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons reflect one shared feature; not tested.
Measurement-dependence of neuron polysemanticity (activation range, explanation scoring) for network neurons; only an SAE pre-latent example is examined.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked R1 to V7 and labeled it supports. That conflates SAE latents with model neurons, and the polysemanticity here is a byproduct of the authors' own architecture. Downgraded to uses_without_test/T4 with no verdicts. Aggregate interpretability and absorption results concern SAE features and are rightly left out.

versions.untested_parts: Image-classifier neurons and mixed visual inputs.
Prevalence of polysemantic MLP neurons in transformer language models and layer differences.
Whether neuron polysemanticity is caused by representing more sparse features than available neurons.
Polysemantic neurons arising without capacity pressure from initialization, regularization, or training noise.
Share of polysemantic neurons across activation functions, architectures, or regularization, and whether that share can be lowered without large performance loss.
Whether canonical polysemantic neurons detect a shared feature or related offshoots, and how often truly unrelated mixtures occur.

The paper examines semantic patterns at different activation ranges for an SAE pre-latent, but does not compare explanation-scoring methods or estimate how often polysemanticity classifications change.

rows.subject: KronSAE pre-latent base 3, head 23 (Gemma-2-2B, layer 12)
rows.operation_detail: Examined interpretations of the pre-latent at different activation-magnitude ranges and compared them with composed post-latent interpretations.

conditions.value: top 75% quantile, top 25% quantile, and interquartile range

rows.value: The comparison-related semantics were associated with the top 75% quantile; spiritual semantics mostly with the top 25% quantile; geographical semantics mainly with the interquartile range.
rows.note: The paper also reports that compositions with extension elements yield more specific interpretations than the polysemous base. It describes these as qualitative observations, not a count of polysemantic neurons.
rows.check: The subject is an SAE encoder pre-latent (base 3, head 23), not a neuron of Gemma-2-2B or any classifier. V7 concerns whether network neurons count as polysemantic depending on the activation range examined, so this row does not measure what V7 names. The value is also a single qualitative example: comparison at top 75% quantile, spiritual at top 25%, geographical in the interquartile range. The authors explain the pre-latent's polysemanticity by their architecture's reduced capacity. Move this to fits_no_version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The semantic pattern attributed to the pre-latent differs across examined activation ranges, supporting an activation-range qualification (R1).
